description: Reported by a Steam Deck player: a T6 Krumpin' fight-row prompt told them to 'Glide {ls} onto da row' even though the row is plain D-pad work. This scenario proves it: it drives the lesson on the pad, asserts the rendered prompt names the D-pad glyph and no longer names LS, picks the fight row with REAL D-pad presses (PadRouter's nested-panel walker steps a row at a time and skips DISABLED stops, so the pad never lands on the enemy's dead row that A could not press), and confirms A on that row really activates the unit — it opens the Epic Challenge offer, because the row is the ATTACHED unit 'Boyz + Warboss' and contains a CHARACTER. Originally written against the separate 'boss_swings' step (step 6 of 8), which is gone now that 19.03 makes the Leader fight inside his squad's one activation; the same pad claims are made at the pick_fighter row instead. The enemy_swings half is unchanged: that prompt must not tell the player to glide the stick either, and the save card grabs pad focus onto its own Roll Saves button.

steps.comment: the harness pins the policy so a device claim can happen at all
LB claims pad mode
A = Continue on the instructor card
Start = End Pile In

THE REPORTED BUG (ported from the removed boss_swings step): the fight-row prompt must name the D-pad glyph (GlyphDB maps {dpad} -> ✚). The row walk is plain D-pad work; the lesson used to tell a Steam Deck player to glide the stick.
...and must NOT still tell the Deck player to glide the left stick (GlyphDB maps {ls} -> LS)
first D-pad press enters HUD_Right panel focus (AISuggestionButton)
second lands on the Boyz row — the pick_fighter prompt's promise

steps.script:
var f = tree.root.get_viewport().gui_get_focus_owner()
return "none" if f == null else str(f.name)
steps.comment: the fight UnitList is a VBox of Buttons (not an ItemList), so it IS on the D-pad focus chain
PadRouter's nested-panel walker steps a ROW at a time and SKIPS disabled stops — the enemy's row is disabled during Player 1's pick and the D-pad never parks on it (A could not press it).

A on the focused row really activated the ATTACHED unit: it contains a CHARACTER, so Epic Challenge is offered (auto-named dialog nodes, so the button is found by text). This is the claim the removed boss_swings block used to make about the Warboss's own row.
the attack dialog's own pad row: down steps the weapon
A assigns it
Start = Fight!
Fast Roll the Boyz' whole activation — this scenario is about step 6, not the dock

19.03: the row the D-pad picked was the whole ATTACHED unit, so ONE activation swung the Boyz AND their Warboss. There is no second Ork row to walk to — which is why the old 'step 6 of 8' boss_swings prompt this scenario was written against no longer exists.
step 7 — the other prompt that used to say 'glide {ls}'
step 7 must not tell the Deck player to glide the stick onto Roll Saves either
the AI takes its alternating activation and parks at the staged hit pause
A steps the enemy's rolls on the dock — exactly what the prompt promises

THE STEP-7 CLAIM: the save card confines pad focus to itself and lands it on its own Roll Saves button (AllocationGroupOverlay._refresh_pad_focus), so the prompt can just say 'press A' — no stick glide needed
